body_markdown:
AI meeting transcription uses artificial intelligence to turn spoken conversations into written text automatically. Instead of taking notes during a video call or trying to remember what was said afterward, teams can create a written record of the conversation as it happens.


For businesses with packed calendars, that changes the role of the meeting itself. People can focus on the conversation while AI captures the details they may need later.


## What is AI call transcription?


AI call transcription is the process of using artificial intelligence to convert spoken words from a phone call, video conference, or online meeting into written text.


The technology listens to the audio, recognizes what people are saying, and creates a transcript of the conversation. Depending on the platform, it can also identify different speakers, add timestamps, organize the text, and make the transcript searchable.


AI meeting transcription applies the same technology specifically to meetings. Instead of assigning someone to take notes, an AI meeting notetaker can capture the conversation automatically.


This is especially useful for businesses that spend a large part of the week in sales calls, project meetings, customer conversations, interviews, or training sessions.


Video conferencing transcription also gives people something a page of handwritten notes can’t: a record of what was actually said. If someone needs to check a detail from Tuesday’s customer meeting, they can go back to the transcript instead of relying on memory or chicken-scratch notes.


## How does AI meeting transcription work?


### 1. Speech recognition converts speech into text


The first step is automatic speech recognition, or ASR.


ASR listens to the audio stream during a live meeting or processes a recording after the meeting ends. It identifies spoken words and converts them into text.


The quality of the audio matters. Background noise, poor microphones, overlapping speakers, accents, and an unreliable connection can all affect transcription accuracy.


### 2. Speaker identification shows who said what


Speaker identification separates different voices in a conversation. Instead of producing one long block of text, the system can organize the transcript around individual speakers.


In a sales call, for example, that can make it easier to separate what the customer said from what the salesperson said. In a team meeting, it helps employees trace a decision or question back to the person who raised it.


### 3. Natural language processing cleans up the transcript


Speech does not look very clean when it is converted directly to text. People pause, repeat themselves, change direction in the middle of a sentence, and use filler words.


Natural language processing, or NLP, can help turn that raw transcript into something easier to read. Depending on the AI meeting notetaker or transcription platform, NLP may add punctuation, improve formatting, organize the conversation, and help create summaries.


## What are the benefits of AI meeting transcription?


The biggest benefit of AI meeting transcription is simple: people don’t have to choose between participating in a conversation and documenting it.


### Meeting transcripts create searchable records


Think about how much useful information is buried inside meetings.


A searchable transcript creates a written record teams can return to later. Instead of watching a full recording or asking coworkers what they remember, employees can search the transcript for a name, topic, decision, or keyword.


For businesses with several meetings every day, those searchable records can become a useful source of company knowledge.


### Automated transcription can save hours of manual work


Grand View Research found that[62% of professionals](https://www.grandviewresearch.com/industry-analysis/us-transcription-market) using its AI meeting assistant saved more than four hours per week. Four hours a week adds up to more than 200 hours over 52 weeks.


That finding fits a broader pattern in workplace AI use.[Microsoft and LinkedIn’s Work Trend Index](https://www.azeusconvene.com/articles/ai-meeting-transcription-software) found that 90% of AI users said the technology helped them save time, while 85% said it helped them focus on their most important work.


For meeting-heavy roles, the benefit is easy to understand. A project manager who attends several calls a day may otherwise spend additional time writing notes, organizing action items, or searching recordings for information.


## How are businesses using AI transcription today?


AI transcription is already being used across industries where conversations create information that needs to be documented, reviewed, or shared.


The medical sector represented[34.7% of the global AI transcription market in 2024](https://market.us/report/ai-transcription-market/) , making it the largest vertical tracked in the research. Common uses include clinical documentation, doctor-patient conversations, medical records, and telehealth.


Healthcare workers have conversations that often need to become documentation. Transcription can help capture those conversations, although healthcare organizations still need to consider accuracy, privacy, security, and regulatory requirements before deciding how transcripts are used or stored.


The same basic need exists in other industries. Financial services teams may need records of client discussions and internal meetings. Government organizations can use transcription for meetings, interviews, and public proceedings. Schools and universities can use video conferencing transcription for lectures, staff meetings, and accessibility. Sales and service teams can use transcripts to revisit customer questions, requirements, and feedback.


## What should businesses look for in AI meeting transcription?


If your team spends its day in a business phone system or video conferencing platform, look at whether AI transcription is already built into that environment. UCaaS with AI transcription can reduce the need to add another standalone tool to every meeting.


Businesses should also look at how transcripts can be accessed, searched, downloaded, and managed. Accuracy matters, but so do security, privacy, user controls, and the quality of the underlying audio.

## AI meeting transcription makes meetings useful after they end


Most meetings create more information than anyone can reasonably write down.


AI meeting transcription helps close that gap. It captures conversations as text, creates a record people can search later, and reduces the time employees spend taking and organizing notes.


That means the meeting does not disappear when everyone clicks “Leave.”
